details: Bitcoin (BTC) saw a 1.88% increase today, June 20, to $63,555, driven by easing geopolitical tensions. However, analysts indicate the bear market remains in control, with BTC rejected from the $67,000-$77,000 resistance zone and a potential deeper move towards $56,000. Negative funding rates and trading below its estimated production cost also highlight underlying market weakness.
title: Bitcoin's Bearish Trend Continues Despite Modest Rebound

details: Concerns have emerged regarding a "slow-burning funding crisis" for Ethereum's core development, potentially requiring $30 million annually. This follows the expiration of the Client Incentive Program and several senior staff departures from the Ethereum Foundation, including co-executive director Hsiao-Wei Wang on June 18. Despite warnings from a former contributor, analyst Tom Lee dismisses these fears as overblown.
title: Ethereum Faces Funding Crisis Warnings Amid Staff Exits

details: Ethereum is showing signs of a potential rebound, with traders closely observing the $1750 price level. A decisive reclaim of this threshold could signal a shift from bearish sentiment, potentially leading to a rally towards $2,100. Institutional activity is also a key factor influencing near-term price movements for ETH.
title: Ethereum Price Bounce Awaits Confirmation Above $1750

details: As Europe's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) July deadline approaches, regulatory impacts on Binance access and USDT liquidity are anticipated. In altcoin markets, some assets saw gains, with Aster surging 3.51% due to a tokenomics overhaul and JST gaining 5% on Tron DeFi narratives. Conversely, others like XLM dropped 9% and ATOM fell 6.86% amid broader crypto deleveraging and a hawkish Federal Reserve stance.
title: EU MiCA Deadline Nears, Altcoins Show Mixed Performance
